podcast.title: Rise in 1991
podcast.body: Spirit of the West began their rise in 1991, becoming part of a new crop of Canadian artists gaining prominence. Their emergence signaled the expansion of the "Can Rock explosion" beyond its initial wave. "1991, so the beginning of the rise of the Barodicad Ladies, Spirit of the West, Sarah McLaughlin, Crash Vegas, Crash Test Dummies, and Grapes of Wrath."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Roots of the 90s CanRock Explosion

podcast.title: Another Roadside Attraction Tourmate
podcast.body: Spirit of the West was a Canadian performer who toured with The Tragically Hip's Another Roadside Attraction festival in 1993, 1995, and 1997. "Tourmates included Canadian performers like Daniel Landwass, Spirit of the West and the Rio Statics."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Origins in Vancouver
podcast.body: This band was formed in Vancouver in 1983, bringing their unique perspective to Celtic music. "Enter to the West was formed in Vancouver in 1983 and put their own spin on things."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: The World's Greatest Drinking Song
podcast.body: One of Spirit of the West's most popular songs within the Celtic diaspora was written during a 1989 tour of England. It originated as a humorous piece about the band's misbehavior in pubs on that tour and was never intended to be recorded. However, an album producer heard it and insisted the group complete it, despite it never being officially released as a single. It has since become one of Canada's, and the world's, greatest drinking songs. "It was never supposed to be recorded, but their producer for one of their albums heard it and demanded that the group finish it. Nevertheless, it was never, ever officially released as a single. Yet somehow, this has become one of Canada's. One of the worlds greatest drinking songs."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Spirit of the West Farewell Performance (2016)
xref.body: Due to the relentless deterioration caused by Alzheimer's, Spirit of the West concluded their career with a farewell performance in 2016. John received immense support from his wife, Jill, throughout his battle with the disease. "Spirit of the West ended with a farewell performance in 2016."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Continued Performance and Stem Cell Treatment
xref.body: John Mann continued performing with Spirit of the West for as long as his deteriorating condition allowed. In 2015, he sought experimental stem cell treatment in Mexico in an attempt to combat the progression of Alzheimer's. "John kept performing as long as he could. There was some stem cell treatment in Mexico in 2015."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Early Onset Alzheimer's Diagnosis
xref.body: John Mann, the singer for Spirit of the West, was diagnosed with early onset Alzheimer's in 2014, when he was in his early 50s. This uncommon form of the disease affects individuals before age 65, accounting for less than 10% of all cases. His diagnosis came while he was in remission from colorectal cancer, which had been diagnosed in 2009. "John was diagnosed with early onset Alzheimer's."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Extensive Touring
xref.body: After the release of their debut album in 2001, Staggered Crossing embarked on tours with notable acts such as Nickelback, The Guess Who, Midnight Oil, Spirit of the West, Blue Rodeo, and Big Sugar, among others. "From there they toured with Nickelback, the Guess Who, Midnight Oil, Spirited the West, Blurodio, Big Sugar and others."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Musician Friends' Benefit Concerts
xref.body: John Mann's musician friends, including members of the Barenaked Ladies, Blue Rodeo, and Sarah McLachlan, regularly organized benefit concerts to help fund his medical treatments. These events often featured collective performances of Spirit of the West classics. "And whenever one of these benefits was held, everybody joins in on this Spirit of the West class."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
